thread:
Maya: kicking off a narrower proposal: tiered burst windows with deterministic billing and a conservative default. Want to collect quick engineering/ops flags before I write the RFC.
Arjun: tl;dr sounds like: short burst window (<=5m) for high-priority bursts, long burst window (up to 24h) for background batch jobs, and explicit billing labels. What are the tiers?
Maya: proposed tiers: 
- "instant" (30s - 5m) for latency-sensitive calls, charged at X rate, non-preemptible for reserved customers
- "day" (1h - 24h) for batch/throughput, cheaper rate, marked preemptible
- "carryover" (soft, up to 48h) auto-applied from unused instant/day credits (cap 15%)
Arjun: implementation notes: need route-level hint with tier tag. Autoscaler must map tier -> allocator behavior. Instant must map to pre-warmed slots. Day tier can be opportunistic. KV cache affinity again is the usual issue.
Ian: runtime constraints: pre-warmed instant capacity expensive. If we reserve too many instant slots for many tenants, utilization drops. We can implement instant as an accelerator token that temporarily bumps priority in the allocator for the request's session rather than static slot reservation.
Sienna: oncall implications: instant non-preemptible increases risk if abused. Suggest rate-limiting per-tenant per-minute and an abuse alert. Also need an eviction audit trail for day-tier preemptions.
Priya: sales perspective: customers want predictable spend. They like tiering if pricing is clear. Need samples: "customer A used 12 instant bursts (avg 60s) -> $Y" and an API to query remaining burst budget.
Dan: finance asks: invoices must show tier-level lines and a month-end summary of carryover credit use. Also: how do refunds/chargebacks work if a marketplace or transfer is introduced later? For now, keep carryover internal only.
Maya: proposal for default gating: instant default = 100 tokens/month for reserved customers; day default = 500 tokens/month; carryover cap = 15% of instant tokens. Opt-out via tenancy settings. Launch gates: RFC, pricing sheet, console counter for remaining tokens, eviction metrics, two internal canaries.
Arjun: config prototype snippet: 
```
burst_tiers:
  instant:
    token_duration_seconds: 300
    default_tokens_per_month: 100
    preemptible: false
  day:
    token_duration_seconds: 86400
    default_tokens_per_month: 500
    preemptible: true
  carryover:
    cap_percent: 15
    ttl_hours: 48
```
Ian: also need allocator knobs: preemption_grace_seconds (suggest 60s), instant_warmup_tokens, global_instant_pool_cap.
Sienna: monitoring: tenant.burst.tokens_remaining.{tier}, tenant.evictions.{tier}.count, tenant.instant.latency.p50/p95, cluster.instant.utilization. Alert: if cluster.instant.utilization < 30% for 24h — consider lowering defaults or opening marketplace.
Priya: customer ask: business-hour protections again. Propose a "business-hours shield" add-on that converts instant tokens to non-preemptible during defined windows. Sales can sell as an SLA premium.
Dan: legal/finance note: any SLA premium must be accompanied by billing uplift and explicit terms in contract. We need a template clause.
Maya: rollout plan: week 0 RFC -> week 2 implement token ledger + API -> week 3 allocator + runtime mapping -> week 4 telemetry + console counters -> week 5 internal canary -> week 8 pilot with 1 enterprise customer (business-hours shield). Owners: Arjun (allocator + autoscaler), Ian (runtime), Sienna (alerts + ops), Priya (sales + pilot), Dan (billing + contracts), Maya (PM).
rfc-bot: RFC draft: https://redwood.infra/rfc/tiered-burst-windows-2026  comments open for 7 days.
Sienna: small ops nit: ensure we have a clear rollback: disable tiered routing and revert to legacy single-burst pool if eviction_rate or latency regressions exceed threshold for 30m.
Arjun: agree. Add circuit breaker in allocator that trips on global_instant_errors > 3% for 10m.
Maya: updating RFC with circuit-breaker, pricing table draft, and pilot checklist. Will post later today. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Priya: I'll prepare a one-page for sales and a customer FAQ.
Ian: will prototype the accelerator token flow and share perf numbers.
Leo (Customer Success): tagging for awareness — happy to help pilot onboarding.
Maya: schedule follow-up review on Friday 10am PT. End.
